sentences.en: It's 1984, and journalist Jack Hitt is walking up Broadway in Manhattan toward Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 那是1984年，记者杰克·希特（Jack Hitt）正走在曼哈顿的百老汇大道上，前往哥伦比亚大学。

sentences.en: Jack is 27 at the time, recently out of grad school and obsessed with American history.
sentences.zh: 当时的杰克27岁，刚从研究生院毕业，对美国历史非常痴迷。

sentences.en: I'm a Constitution nerd, you know, and my girlfriend and I've decided to write a book about marginalized figures in American history.
sentences.zh: “我是一个宪法迷，你知道的，我和我女朋友决定写一本关于美国历史上边缘人物的书。”

sentences.en: So on this particularly romantic day, Jack was on his way to do some research on the Revolutionary War in the stacks of Butler Library.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个特别浪漫的日子里，杰克正要去巴特勒图书馆（Butler Library）的书库里做一些关于美国独立战争的研究。

sentences.en: Butler Library is one of these libraries when you walk in the front door, it looks like it has about like four or five stories, but it's actually like 12 stories underground, too.
sentences.zh: 巴特勒图书馆是那种你从正门走进去，看起来只有四五层楼高，但实际上地下还有12层楼的图书馆。

sentences.en: So I'm down like in the ninth floor, and you know that setting, right?
sentences.zh: “所以我当时在地下九层，你知道那种环境吧？”

sentences.en: It's just books, wall-to-wall books, and there's nobody down there.
sentences.zh: 到处都是书，四面墙都是书，而且那里一个人也没有。

sentences.en: It's this wonderful feeling of come off the elevator or walk down the stairs.
sentences.zh: “那种感觉很奇妙，当你走出电梯或走下楼梯时。”

sentences.en: You're in this like just dark envelope of books, and each aisle is only illuminated by this little 15-minute timer that you turn when you walk down it.
sentences.zh: “你就像置身于一个黑暗的书籍包裹之中，每条过道只由一个你走进去时打开的15分钟定时器照亮。”

sentences.en: And so I'm heading down towards the American Revolution section.
sentences.zh: “所以我正朝美国独立战争区走去。”

sentences.en: On his mind is one particular figure from the American Revolution, someone Jack thought history had almost entirely overlooked.
sentences.zh: 他心里想的是美国独立战争中的一个特定人物，一个杰克认为几乎被历史完全遗忘的人。

sentences.en: We'd come across this guy named James Otis, who had written this sort of inflammatory pamphlet really early on, the early 1760s, you know,
sentences.zh: “我们偶然发现了这个叫詹姆斯·奥蒂斯（James Otis）的人，他在18世纪60年代初写过一本煽动性的小册子，你知道的，”

sentences.en: a good 10 or 15 years before the Declaration of Independence.
Some people say, you know, this is the document that sort of got the ball rolling.
sentences.zh: “有些人说，这正是开启这一切的文件。”

sentences.en: Jack was fired up about this pamphlet.
sentences.zh: 杰克对这本小册子感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And if you're thinking this is kind of like a brochure that you get at a doctor's office, you know, with a diagram of the food pyramid, think again.
sentences.zh: “如果你以为这就像你在医生办公室拿到的那种带有食物金字塔图表的宣传册，那你就想错了。”

sentences.en: Pamphlets were how big ideas were spread at the time.
sentences.zh: 小册子是当时传播重大思想的方式。

sentences.en: They could be printed quickly and disseminated widely.
sentences.zh: 它们可以被快速印刷并广泛传播。

sentences.en: And it was also the place where you might have a hot take, right?
sentences.zh: “而且这也是你可能会发表尖锐观点的地方，对吧？”

sentences.en: So think of the famous pamphlets that we all learn later in American history, Thomas Paine's Common Sense or Letters from a Farmer in Pennsylvania by John Dickinson.
sentences.zh: 所以想想我们后来在美国历史课上学到的那些著名小册子，比如托马斯·潘恩（Thomas Paine）的《常识》，或者约翰·迪金森（John Dickinson）的《宾夕法尼亚农民来信》。

sentences.en: They're the ones that, you know, that lasted and were famous.
sentences.zh: 它们就是那些流传下来并广为人知的作品。

sentences.en: And that's why my girlfriend at the time and I wanted to write this book, because Otis's pamphlet deserves to be that famous.
sentences.zh: “这就是当时我和我女朋友想写这本书的原因，因为奥蒂斯的小册子理应享有同样的盛名。”

sentences.en: But what made the story kind of great for us is that things go sideways for Otis.
sentences.zh: 但让这个故事对我们来说很棒的一点是，奥蒂斯的事情后来急转直下。
那就像莎士比亚的剧作一样。

sentences.en: A man, you know, soaring into greatness, crashing into unbelievable humiliation and then madness.
sentences.zh: 一个男人，你知道的，从迈向伟大，到坠入难以置信的羞辱，最后陷入疯狂。

sentences.en: And, you know, of course, I romanced the idea that, you know, these dangerous ideas that he was entertaining so early on, you know, had taken him over the edge.
sentences.zh: “而且，当然，我浪漫化地认为，他那么早就开始思考的那些危险思想，让他走到了崩溃的边缘。”

sentences.en: So without the Internet to rely on, Jack is looking for a book that might tell him more about this tragic proto-founding father and his inflammatory pamphlet.
sentences.zh: 所以，在没有互联网可以依赖的情况下，杰克正在寻找一本能告诉他更多关于这位悲剧性的“开国元勋先驱”及其煽动性小册子的书。

sentences.en: And I'm poking through the books, looking for which ones I should check out.
sentences.zh: “我翻找着书架，看看该借哪几本。”

sentences.en: And I look behind one of the books and I see that there's something back there, a thin volume, hand-sewn binding.
sentences.zh: “我往书的后面看了一眼，发现后面有东西，一本薄薄的、手工装订的书。”

sentences.en: Pull out some books, pull this thing out.
sentences.zh: 把一些书抽出来，把这东西拿出来。

sentences.en: And this is the pamphlet that James Otis wrote.
sentences.zh: 这就是詹姆斯·奥蒂斯写的那本小册子。

sentences.en: And this is an original copy.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一本原版拷贝。

sentences.en: It's a 1764 edition of the pamphlet that made him famous.
sentences.zh: 这是让他成名的那本小册子的1764年版本。

sentences.en: My first thought, of course, is I should steal this.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个念头当然是：我应该把它偷走。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking that in the most virtuous way.
sentences.zh: 而且我当时是以最“高尚”的方式这么想的。

sentences.en: They don't know what they have.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道自己拥有什么。

sentences.en: It's rotting into dust back there behind these books.
sentences.zh: 它在这些书后面腐烂成灰。

sentences.en: It's the Magna Carta of America.
I know what I'm holding in my hand.
sentences.zh: 我知道我手里拿着的是什么。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it just sit back there and turn into dust over the next hundred years if I don't save it?
sentences.zh: 如果我不拯救它，它难道不会在接下来的几百年里一直待在那里变成灰烬吗？

sentences.en: It's the only moral option is to take it.
sentences.zh: 唯一的道德选择就是把它带走。

sentences.en: And then the light timer cut off and I was plunged into darkness.
sentences.zh: 然后灯光定时器关掉了，我陷入了一片黑暗。

sentences.en: Matching the darkness of your soul.
sentences.zh: 和你灵魂的黑暗相呼应。

sentences.en: So, of course, I crab walked out of there,
sentences.zh: 所以，我当然是像螃蟹一样爬了出去，

sentences.en: took the elevator to the ground floor and up to the sixth floor into the bright light of the rare books division and handed it to the curator.
sentences.zh: 坐电梯到了一楼，又上了六楼，走进珍本部的明亮灯光下，把它交给了馆长。

sentences.en: And I told her, this jewel of the American Revolution has been rotting away in the stacks.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她，这颗美国独立战争的明珠一直烂在书库里。

sentences.en: And I hope that they will take it and preserve it.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们能把它收好并妥善保存。

sentences.en: And that's where it is today.
sentences.zh: 这就是它今天所在的地方。

sentences.en: But James Otis is still sort of in that hidden place in American history.
sentences.zh: 但詹姆斯·奥蒂斯在美国历史上仍然处于那种隐秘的角落。

sentences.en: To tell the story of James Otis and his seminal pamphlet is to tell the story of a bolt from the blue.
sentences.zh: 讲述詹姆斯·奥蒂斯和他那本开创性小册子的故事，就是讲述一个突如其来的惊雷的故事。

sentences.en: A spark that would electrify the American Revolution.
sentences.zh: 一颗点燃美国独立战争的火花。

sentences.en: Before the Declaration of Independence was even a twinkle in the founding father's eyes, there was James Otis.
sentences.zh: 在《独立宣言》甚至还没在开国元勋们的脑海中闪现之前，就已经有了詹姆斯·奥蒂斯。

sentences.en: And you could argue that the story of this pamphlet is the story of the founding document of the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，这本小册子的故事就是美利坚合众国建国文件的故事。

sentences.en: From 99% Invisible and BBC Studios, this is a history of the United States in 100 Objects.
sentences.zh: 来自99% Invisible和BBC Studios，这是《100件物品中的美国历史》。

sentences.en: And today, Jack Hitt is back with the Otis pamphlet, America's forgotten Magna Carta and the life of the tragic hero who wrote it.
sentences.zh: 今天，杰克·希特带着奥蒂斯的小册子回来了，这是美国被遗忘的《大宪章》，以及写下它的悲剧英雄的一生。

sentences.en: The story of this pamphlet begins around 15 years before the Revolutionary War, in 1761, in the tiny hamlet of Boston, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 这本小册子的故事始于独立战争前约15年的1761年，在马萨诸塞州波士顿的一个小村庄里。

sentences.en: You know, at the time, Boston is this tiny little port town, population 16,000.
sentences.zh: “你知道，当时波士顿只是个小港口城镇，人口16000人。”

sentences.en: So it's like a large university.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像一所大型大学。

sentences.en: You practically know everybody on campus.
sentences.zh: 你几乎认识校园里的每一个人。

sentences.en: And certainly the people in power all knew each other.
sentences.zh: 当然，当权者们也都互相认识。

sentences.en: The city is so small, you could walk from one side of it to the other in under an hour,
sentences.zh: 这座城市很小，你可以在不到一小时内从一头走到另一头，

sentences.en: during which time you might hear boats from Boston Harbor creaking and knocking into the docks.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，你可能会听到波士顿港的船只在码头上吱吱作响和碰撞的声音。

sentences.en: You might encounter pigs loose in the street.
sentences.zh: 你可能会遇到街上乱跑的猪。

sentences.en: And if you weren't like in a church, you were probably in a tavern.
sentences.zh: 如果你不在教堂里，那你可能就在酒馆里。

sentences.en: And just remember, you know, we're talking about a time when no one is thinking of rebellion.
sentences.zh: 记住，我们谈论的是一个没人想到要反叛的时代。

sentences.en: These are British citizens in Boston, 1761, a full 15 years before the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 这些是1761年的波士顿英国公民，距离《独立宣言》还有整整15年。

sentences.en: And at the time, you know, they're mostly merchants trying to make a living and make something of their new life in America.
sentences.zh: 当时，他们大多是试图谋生并在这片美国新土地上有所作为的商人。

sentences.en: But the living the merchants were making wasn't always strictly legal.
sentences.zh: 但商人们的生计并不总是完全合法的。

sentences.en: There's a there's a good bit of smuggling and everybody kind of knows it, you know,
sentences.zh: “走私现象相当普遍，每个人心里都有数，你知道的，”

sentences.en: and a lot of it was about getting cheap French molasses out of the Caribbean and into the rum kegs.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分是关于把加勒比海廉价的法国糖蜜弄进朗姆酒桶里。

sentences.en: One of the big trades in the New England colonies was making rum, but the cheapest molasses was from the French Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 新英格兰殖民地的大宗贸易之一是制造朗姆酒，但最便宜的糖蜜来自法属加勒比地区。

sentences.en: So to get around heavy tariffs, merchants smuggled it in and London was tired of it.
sentences.zh: 为了绕过高额关税，商人们将其走私进来，而伦敦对此感到厌倦。

sentences.en: And they wanted those tax dollars or I suppose those tax shillings.
sentences.zh: 他们想要那些税款，或者我应该说是那些税收先令。

sentences.en: And so to catch these smugglers, London has issued these new kinds of search warrants called writs of assistance and they're they're blanket warrants.
sentences.zh: 为了抓住这些走私者，伦敦发布了一种新的搜查令，称为“协助令”（writs of assistance），它们是全权搜查令。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't need any evidence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你根本不需要任何证据。

sentences.en: You can come aboard a ship day or night.
sentences.zh: 你可以随时随地登上船只。

sentences.en: You can go into a house or a warehouse anytime during the day with the barest of suspicions.
sentences.zh: 你可以在白天任何时候，仅凭最微小的怀疑就进入一所房子或仓库。

sentences.en: And the reason they're called writs of assistance is the other aspect of them is that they any agent who holds this piece of paper can kind of dragoon anyone into accompanying them on one of these searches.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫“协助令”，是因为它的另一个方面是，任何持有这张纸的代理人都可以强迫任何人陪同他们进行搜查。

sentences.en: I mean, if they stop you, one of these customs agents stops you and says, you have to help me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们拦住你，这些海关代理人拦住你说，你必须帮我。

sentences.en: And so you have this like little mob practically coming into people's places and searching and looking for smuggled goods and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有这种几乎像暴徒一样的小团体进入人们的地方，搜查并寻找走私货物等等。

sentences.en: And the kicker was that the customs agents also had a financial incentive.
sentences.zh: 最绝的是，海关代理人还有经济动机。

sentences.en: They got a cut of whatever they found.
sentences.zh: 他们能从查获的物品中分得一杯羹。

sentences.en: So you've got agents prowling around town more and more like thugs and everyone is scared and on edge.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到代理人在城里像流氓一样四处游荡，每个人都感到害怕和紧张。

sentences.en: And ostensibly the owner or the holder of this writ of assistance is an agent of the British government in some way.
sentences.zh: 表面上，这种“协助令”的所有者或持有者在某种程度上是英国政府的代理人。

sentences.en: These writs are executed, you know, by authority from London by the court in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 这些搜查令是由伦敦授权，通过马萨诸塞州的法院执行的。

sentences.en: So you really have this sort of like wonderful tempest in a teapot where you have, you know, the authorities are angry because duties are definitely being avoided.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实有这种美妙的“茶杯里的风暴”，当局很生气，因为关税确实被规避了。

sentences.en: Money is not going into the king's coffers.
sentences.zh: 钱没有进入国王的国库。

sentences.en: And then you have the merchants and they're also furious about, you know, the abuse of these blanket warrants.
sentences.zh: 然后商人们也对滥用这些全权搜查令感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And so, you know, everybody's like ready for a courtroom battle.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都准备好进行一场法庭大战了。

sentences.en: And so the merchants bring a lawsuit and charge that, you know, these writs of assistance are illegal.
sentences.zh: 于是商人们提起诉讼，指控这些“协助令”是非法的。

sentences.en: That's now called the old state house in Boston.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在波士顿的旧州议会大厦。

sentences.en: And there were five British judges sitting in wigs and red robes at the front.
sentences.zh: 前面坐着五位戴着假发、穿着红袍的英国法官。

sentences.en: And so you can imagine the public is permitted to come.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，公众是被允许进入的。

sentences.en: And so the place is packed.
First, the British government's lawyer gets up and makes the expected case in favor of the writs.
sentences.zh: 首先，英国政府的律师站起来，提出了支持搜查令的预期论点。

sentences.en: Parliament authorized these search warrants and Parliament's word is law.
sentences.zh: 议会授权了这些搜查令，议会的话就是法律。

sentences.en: Standard, you know, defense of the writs.
sentences.zh: 这是对搜查令的标准辩护。

sentences.en: Then it's the merchants turn to try to convince the judges that the writs are illegal.
sentences.zh: 接下来轮到商人们试图说服法官这些搜查令是非法的。

sentences.en: And the first lawyer for the merchants gets up.
sentences.zh: 商人们的第一位律师站了起来。

sentences.en: A guy with a fabulous Dickensian name, Oxenbridge Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 一个有着狄更斯式美妙名字的人，奥克森布里奇·撒切尔（Oxenbridge Thatcher）。

sentences.en: Oxenbridge makes an equally predictable case on the opposite side.
sentences.zh: 奥克森布里奇在对立面提出了同样可预测的论点。

sentences.en: But he makes this very tidy argument about the writs, you know, citing precedent and so on.
sentences.zh: 但他对搜查令提出了非常整洁的论点，引用了先例等等。

sentences.en: So far, the packed audience doesn't seem moved.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，挤满的观众似乎并没有被打动。

sentences.en: But the merchants have a second lawyer too.
sentences.zh: 但商人们还有第二位律师。

sentences.en: A hotshot, hotheaded man who just joined their team.
sentences.zh: 一个刚加入他们团队的、炙手可热、脾气火爆的人。

sentences.en: Now, I just got to try to describe James Otis to you.
sentences.zh: 现在，我得试着向你描述一下詹姆斯·奥蒂斯。

sentences.en: And he was sort of known as a really hot shot kind of badass lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他以一个非常厉害、非常强硬的律师而闻名。

sentences.en: He defended pirates in Nova Scotia.
sentences.zh: 他曾在新斯科舍省为海盗辩护。

sentences.en: There were some young guys that went rioting on Guy Fawkes Day.
sentences.zh: 有一些年轻人在盖伊·福克斯日（Guy Fawkes Day）闹事。

sentences.en: He took their case, you know.
And his friends had a nickname for him.
sentences.zh: 他的朋友们给他起了一个绰号。

sentences.en: You have to earn that one.
And just to complicate things for Furio a little more,
sentences.zh: 为了让“狂暴者”的情况更复杂一点，

sentences.en: he had a personal history with the Chief Justice.
sentences.zh: 他和首席大法官之间还有一段私人恩怨。
一个叫托马斯·哈钦森（Thomas Hutchinson）的人。

sentences.en: Who, at the time, had just been appointed by the governor.
And the man he had passed over for this job,
sentences.zh: 而那个被总督忽略、没得到这个职位，

sentences.en: that the governor had passed over and given to Hutchinson,
sentences.zh: 被总督跳过并把职位给了哈钦森的人，
正是詹姆斯·奥蒂斯的父亲。

sentences.en: So, it's no secret, these two don't like each other.
sentences.zh: 所以，这已经不是什么秘密了，这两个人互相看不顺眼。
但他们之间也存在根本性的分歧。

sentences.en: Otis quit his job to take this case.
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯辞去了工作来接手这个案子。

sentences.en: Until days before the trial, he was working for the government side,
sentences.zh: 直到审判前几天，他还在为政府一方工作，

sentences.en: meaning he should have been arguing in favor of the Ritz.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他本该为“里茨”号辩护。

sentences.en: But he quit the job and dramatically offered to represent the merchants for free.
sentences.zh: 但他辞去了工作，并戏剧性地主动提出免费为商人们代理。

sentences.en: Now, you can say, you know, he did this for principal,
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以说，你知道，他是出于原则才这么做的，

sentences.en: or he did this because he still steamed about his old man.
sentences.zh: 或者是因为他还在为他父亲的事耿耿于怀。

sentences.en: So, Otis takes to the floor, and he speaks for five hours.
sentences.zh: 于是，奥蒂斯走上台，足足讲了五个小时。

sentences.en: Now, let me just say something about five hours.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我来谈谈这五个小时。

sentences.en: I think people forget that way before television and radio,
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们忘了，在电视和广播出现之前，
在电报、甚至杂志出现之前，

sentences.en: oratory was a whole other kind of, you know, public entertainment, really.
sentences.zh: 演说其实是另一种完全不同的公共娱乐活动。

sentences.en: I always love to remind people that, you know,
